text:
clara ng: hey team, new hire here — just unboxed an M1 Pro and ran the Kandji ABM flow. Kandji says 'Enrolled' but a bunch of things are blocked: Homebrew installs fail with permission errors, the Intel-only toolchain prompts to install Rosetta but it errors out, macOS shows 'System extension blocked' for our VPN helper, and when I try to enable FileVault it fails with 'Escrow failed: 403 Forbidden'. Okta device trust marks it non-compliant. anyone seen this pattern? who should I ping? :wave:
it-ops: welcome Clara! quick questions: which network were you on during setup (home vs RWD-Corp)? can you paste outputs of these (don't post full serials, last 4 ok if needed):
```
profiles status -type configuration
sudo fdesetup status
systemextensionsctl list
sw_vers
```
also which package/path fail for Homebrew (error text helps)
roberto gomez: two quick notes — Rosetta install sometimes requires network to Apple's servers and also requires the installer binary to run as root; MDM can also block automatic Rosetta installs. if systemextensions are blocked you'll see VPN helper not allowed under Privacy & Security.
clara ng: i set it up on my home wifi. outputs:
profiles status -type configuration: Enrolled to kandji: true; com.redwood.mdm present; com.redwood.security: not installed
sudo fdesetup status: FileVault is Off
systemextensionsctl list: No managed extensions allowed; 1 blocked extension: com.vpn.vendor.networkextension (status: blocked by user)
sw_vers: ProductName: macOS Ventura 13.6
Homebrew error when installing: "mkdir /opt/homebrew: permission denied" and the Rosetta prompt says 'Installation failed - installer encountered an error'. Okta shows 'device not compliant (missing device profile)'.
it-ops: thanks — missing com.redwood.security explains Okta. home wifi can block SCEP/PKI in some edge cases or fail during the Bootstrap phase. try these steps in order: 1) Connect to RWD-Corp SSID (or tether to phone), 2) in System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> General click 'Allow' for any system extension banners, 3) visit https://kandji.redwood/setup-cert in Safari to force cert install, 4) run `profiles renew -type enrollment` and `profiles status -type configuration` again. if the Rosetta installer still fails, run `sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license` (we might be able to push this remotely).
roberto gomez: small add — Homebrew on Apple Silicon wants /opt/homebrew writable by your user; if Kandji applied a restrictive file ownership profile it can block. after joining corp network and cert install, we can temporarily grant you admin to fix ownership and approve system extensions. we prefer to do admin windows of 2 hours. want that?
clara ng: tried connecting to RWD-Corp (tethered to phone) and visited the Kandji URL; got an 'Untrusted Certificate' dialog first but allowed it. ran the renew command — now profiles shows com.redwood.security present. re-ran Rosetta command `sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license` and it still failed with 'installer exit code 64'. system says there's a blocked system extension popup — i clicked allow. Homebrew still errors with same mkdir permission denied. FileVault still errors: 'Escrow failed: 403 Forbidden'. last 4 serial: 9D4F
infra-bot: automated hint: 403 from escrow often means the device attempted escrow before SCEP cert or client cert was present. Wait ~5-10 minutes after profile install and ensure network connectivity to our escrow endpoint (outbound TLS). Also check Keychain Access -> Certificates for 'Redwood Corporate CA'.
it-ops: granted 2-hour temporary admin for Clara starting now. pushing a remediation to set correct /opt/homebrew ownership and push the com.redwood.security profile if needed. please stay online for ~5 minutes. ticket NH-20260412-88 created and assigned to endpoint.
roberto gomez: pushed a small script via Kandji that will chown /opt/homebrew to your user, install Rosetta, and trigger a profile renewal. you'll see a Kandji action notification; approve it and then try `brew install git` as a smoke test.
clara ng: approved Kandji action, script ran and reported 'rosetta installed', chown successful. tried `brew install git` -> works now. re-ran `sudo fdesetup enable` and the UI asked to enable FileVault; after accepting it shows 'Escrow in progress' then 'Escrow completed'. Okta shows compliant after a sync a few minutes later. thanks all!
it-ops: glad it worked — closing NH-20260412-88. notes for runbook: if Rosetta install fails with exit 64 during MDM bootstrap, check network, ensure CA cert present, and consider remote Rosetta push + temp admin. leaving a quick doc link: https://intranet.redwood/it/onboarding/mac-rosetta-kandji (internal). :white_check_mark:
